3. A set of structured metadata, consisting of:

         the publication year, represented as an integer in a given range [2012, 2022];
         the publication month, represented as an integer in {1, . . . , 12}.

    Each news entry is associated with one or more semantic categories (e.g.,
politics, economy, health, lifestyle). Let K = 18 denote the number of possible
labels. The targets are represented as a binary matrix:

                                  Y ∈ {0, 1}N ×K
   where:

    Yik = 1 if the i-th sample is associated with subject k;

    Yik = 0 otherwise.

                                          1

The minimum number of subjects per news entry is 2 and the maximum is 3, with
an average of 2.27. The K subjects appear at least in 1000 and at most in 4000
news.

   Design a deep neural network capable of predicting the news labels,
starting from the available data.
   Take 5 minutes to think about the problem, then provide a clear answer to
each of the following points. Please, write in a READABLE way.

  1. MODEL CHOICE. Which architecture do you consider the most appropriate
     for this task, and briefly explain why;

  2. INPUT
        a How to (if) preprocess input data;
        b Which is, after the preprocessing step (if any), the input of the model,
          and how is it represented (e.g., shape, input value domain);

  3. OUTPUT and LOSS. How would you design the output layer and which loss
     function would you use to train your model? Why?;

5. MODEL EVALUATION. How would you assess (in which setting and how)
     the generalization capabilities of the model on unseen data?

   HOW TO ANSWER

    Keep the same numbering of the questions, and their subitems as

    Motivate your choices. Provide technical/mathematical descriptions when

     component of the vector is in [0, 1], representing the fraction of the
     width and of the height respectively. c1 = 0(resp. 1) means the
     bottom-left corner of box lies on the left (resp. right) border of the
     figure;

3. Further, we have some additional labelled images which have no bounding
     box information, respectively 26, 2, and 0 for a1, a2 and a3 classes.

ASSIGNMENT
Design a deep neural network model trained to predict:

  1. The class of the image (which animal it contains among a1, a2, a3),
     assuming any image contains just one of these three animals;

  2. The location of the bounding box, intended as a vector of 4 coordinates,
     as described above.
